answer.evidence: Rows 1-12 are a wide roof of orange and green tarp strips, 12 rows tall, and are the top plane (c). A gold eave edge line sits at rows 13-14, followed by dark shadow behind the hanging cloths from row 15. Below it is an open front of about 16 rows (15-30) with cloths, poles and rugs on the ground. The silhouette is a steady 46-48 px wide, with no side face. The roof is more than a rim, and the front face is 3+ rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: Measured facts: the candidate has 19 visible tones per tile, against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well, so it is at reference level. Near-flat coverage is 4%, which is low (the stall is 13%). Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted and not a black sticker line. By eye, the tarp roof is built from strips in orange, green and teal with a dark brown or red-brown edge. The hanging cloths in pink, yellow, blue and white add variety. The rolled rugs and bundles below are small, however, and each material ramp looks shallow, about 3-4 steps per tarp strip and per cloth. The roof strips are close to flat blocks with only a few dots of highlight. The well and stall references show 5-6 steps with per-tile highlights and grain. The candidate is therefore a little flatter in craft than the references, even though it is busy overall. The number of tones comes mostly from having many different materials, not from deep ramps on each one. A careful artist would likely ask for more shading on the tarp strips and for grain on the ground bundles before accepting it next to the stall.
